standard_ref: docs/standards/AUTONOMOUS_EXECUTION_STANDARD.md Section 15 (cross-project handoff persistence) and Section 15.1 (reverse handoff)
shape_note: This file is a handoff-chain artifact, not a full AES execution record. It does not itself contain 'requirements' / 'overall_delivery' / etc. top-level fields, and is not expected to satisfy scripts/validate_autonomous_execution_record.py's execution-record shape checks. It exists to make the Section 15 handoff_id/execution_id/parent_execution_id/... shape concrete across three real, already-executed pilot legs (Phase 2 Codex, Phase 4 Analytics) plus one new root [Thinking] execution, per docs/pilots/AES_CROSS_PROJECT_PILOT.md deliverable 1.

root_execution.objective: Define and track a cross-project analysis-to-fix chain: identify (via [Analytics]) that the Phase 4 synthetic MART reconciliation required a corrective fix, and demonstrate (via [Codex]) that AES-tracked identity (execution_id, requirement_ids, defect_ids, iteration references, evidence_refs, acceptance snapshot, authority status) survives the [Thinking] -> [Analytics] -> [Codex] -> Judge handoff chain end to end.
root_execution.note: This root execution is deliberately minimal: it is the orchestration/tracking record for the pilot itself, not a full Standard/Full-risk AES execution record. Its only role is to be the parent_execution_id anchor for handoff-crossproject-pilot-001 below.

acceptance_snapshot.reason: Root [Thinking] execution defines the cross-project objective and hands the analysis scope to [Analytics]; no [Analytics] work has started yet at the moment this handoff is issued.

handoffs.fulfillment_note: Fulfilled by the real, already-executed Phase 4 Analytics pilot: docs/autonomous_execution/examples/pilot_evidence/analytics_pilot.json, execution_id exec-aes-phase4-analytics-pilot-001. Its req-001 (QoQ revenue reconciliation must match DATA_CONTRACT.md, no cancelled-order leakage) is the real requirement carried forward as satisfying this handoff's analysis objective.
handoffs.gap_observed: The fulfilling execution (exec-aes-phase4-analytics-pilot-001) was authored in Phase 4 before this Phase 5 root execution existed, so that record's own parent_execution_id field is stored as null, not exec-aes-crossproject-pilot-001 -- it cannot honestly be edited retroactively without altering frozen Phase 4 evidence. Canonical Section 15 persistence is asserted here, at the handoff-array level, via fulfilled_by_execution_id rather than by rewriting the frozen Phase 4 record. This is a real gap between the canonical contract (parent link lives on the child record) and current practice (link only exists in the pilot's own tracking artifact).

acceptance_snapshot.reason: Analytics leg complete: analytics_pilot.json overall_delivery is pass, def-001 (cancelled-order revenue leakage into the MART total) was registered and resolved within the Analytics execution itself (iter-001 -> iter-002). A related code-side fix demonstration is handed to [Codex] to complete the cross-project chain for this pilot.

handoffs.fulfillment_note: Fulfilled by the real, already-executed Phase 2 Codex pilot: docs/autonomous_execution/examples/pilot_evidence/codex_corrective_loop_pilot.json, execution_id exec-aes-codex-pilot-001. Its def-pilot-001 corrective-loop (registered at iter-001, resolved at iter-002, one-fix policy respected) demonstrates the code-side fix leg of this chain.
handoffs.gap_observed: Phase 2's def-pilot-001 (clamp_percentage missing lower-bound clamp) is NOT literally causally derived from Phase 4's def-001 (MART reconciliation leakage) -- they are two independently-fixtured pilot defects, produced on two separate, unrelated branches/fixtures. This handoff record links them purely to pilot the cross-project identity-preservation mechanics required by docs/standards/AUTONOMOUS_EXECUTION_STANDARD.md Section 15 (which is what docs/pilots/AES_CROSS_PROJECT_PILOT.md asks this Phase 5 pilot to exercise), not to assert a real data/causal dependency between the two defects -- that would be a fabrication. Also carries the same parent_execution_id gap as hop 1: exec-aes-codex-pilot-001's own frozen record stores parent_execution_id: null.

handoffs.shape_note: This entry follows the Section 15.1 reverse-handoff shape (Judge/QA back to executor is the canonical direction; this is the mirror -- executor surfacing its resolved state to Judge for a not-yet-performed review). parent_execution_id and authority_status are additive fields beyond the literal 15.1 yaml block, included here for full chain traceability back to the root pilot execution.
handoffs.honesty_note: No live Judge pass occurred in this pilot run. judge_verdict is honestly recorded as not_run, matching the real codex_corrective_loop_pilot.json record's own judge_verdict field (also not_run, see that file's top-level 'judge_verdict' and 'qa_status'). This reverse handoff records the Codex leg's resolved-defect state (def-pilot-001, status: resolved, one-fix policy respected, revalidated by val-pilot-002/003/004) being surfaced to Judge as the next owner -- it is not a claim that Judge review happened. Fabricating a pass here would violate the authority-separation principle in docs/standards/AUTONOMOUS_EXECUTION_STANDARD.md Section 15.1 ('a handoff must never drop ... authority status') by blurring not_run into pass.
